test.name: Refine a Find A Grave memorial citation with the reliability half (src_002)
test.description: src_002 is a Find A Grave memorial for Bridget Fallon. A memorial is a compiled, contributor-authored page, not an original record — its reliability depends on who made it and what they based it on. The extended FindAGrave template #2542 adds carries the contributor, the created/last-modified date, and the source of the source. The rough before-state citation names FindAGrave.com as creator; the contributor, the last-modified date, and a stated source of the source (an obituary) are all on file.

input.delegation:
Refine the citation on src_002, Bridget Fallon's Find A Grave memorial.

sourceId: src_002
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The citation must follow the Find A Grave pattern — Find A Grave, memorial [number], [person] ([dates]), [cemetery], [location] — and then carry the reliability half: the contributor (Mark T. Steward), the created/last-modified date (last modified 3 February 2019), and the source of the source (the 1921 obituary in the Dubuque Telegraph-Herald). All three are on file in the before-state and must appear.

who should not be 'FindAGrave.com' (the repository/access point). A memorial is contributor-authored; the citation must make clear who created the page and what it was based on, which is the point of the reliability half.

A memorial cited with only its number, person, cemetery and access date — omitting the contributor, the date, and the stated source of the source — fails Mills's reliability test on exactly the shape this system most often produces.

Source fidelity: the contributor, the last-modified date, and the obituary source of the source are all on file, so grade them being carried. Do not invent a contributor, a date, or a source of the source not on file (in persisted fields or output.text_response); where a memorial does not state one, an unknown-marker is correct.
Must NOT change source_classification, must NOT create a new source entry (refine src_002 in place), and must call validate_research_schema after writing.
